C08-M07-L08-F1.title: R7 macro_doc_then_shell: correlating two log sources
C08-M07-L08-F1.caption: How R7 joins a macro-document download and an Office-spawned shell on the same host within 600 seconds to raise one higher-confidence alert.
C08-M07-L08-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom graph. A blue node Proxy event (URL ends .docm or .xlsm) and a slate node Sysmon event 1 (Word or Excel starts PowerShell or cmd.exe) both point into a violet node Join on host (same workstation). That points into a violet node 0 to 600 s after download (integer seconds). From it, a solid arrow labelled pass leads to a dark node R7 alert (host, user, URL, both times), which points to a green node Triage queue (RULE_META R7: 3, 0.9). A dashed arrow labelled fail leads to a red node No alert (other host, before download, or later than 600 s).

nodes.label: Sysmon event 1
nodes.sub: Word or Excel starts PowerShell or cmd.exe

nodes.sub: other host, before download, or later than 600 s

C08-M07-L08-F1.note: On the Banyan data the pair is WS-104: invoice.docm at 06:12:00, Word starts PowerShell at 06:14:00 (120 s), giving one hit.

C08-M07-L08-F2.title: R7 time window: floating-point bug versus integer fix
C08-M07-L08-F2.caption: The first version of R7's window dropped a spawn at exactly ten minutes; computing the gap in integer seconds fixed it.
C08-M07-L08-F2.alt: Two code panels. Red panel Buggy: float minutes, with lines AND p.ts >= d.ts and AND (julianday(p.ts) - julianday(d.ts)) * 1440 <= 10, then the computed gap for 10 minutes, 10.000000074505806, and the result: <= 10 is false, so the boundary chain is dropped. Green panel Fixed: integer seconds, with lines AND CAST(strftime('%s', p.ts) AS INTEGER) minus CAST(strftime('%s', d.ts) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 0 AND 600, then the computed gap, 600, and the result: 0 <= 600 <= 600, so the boundary chain is kept.
C08-M07-L08-F2.note: Only the boundary test (spawn at exactly 600 s) caught the bug; every other test passed with the buggy version.
